title: How to Organize and Keep Files from Freelance Projects
h1: How to organize and keep files from freelance projects
description: What files to request at the end of a project, how to organize and back them up, keep licenses and access records, and hand work over to someone new.
intro: When a freelance project ends, the files you receive are what you keep. Months later, you may need to update a logo, edit a video, change website text or brief a new freelancer. If source files are missing, licenses lost or accounts in someone else's name, small updates turn into expensive rework. A little organization at the end of each project protects your investment. This article explains what to request, how to store it and how to hand work over smoothly.

faq.a: The editable working files, such as layered design files or video project files, used to create the final output.
Not always. Check the package and ask before ordering if you need them.

faq.q: Where should I store project files?
faq.a: In a cloud folder owned by your business, with a backup in a second location.

faq.q: What should I do with licenses?
faq.a: Save them with the files they relate to, noting what each allows.

faq.q: How do I hand work to a new freelancer?
faq.a: Share the organized folder, guidelines, access through new accounts and a short handover note.
